rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation changes loop from i<4 to i<=4, adding 5th iteration. Thread T with idx=N*4 processes position N*4+4 at i=4. Thread T+1 with idx=(N+1)*4 processes same position at i=0. Both compute hardtanh(input[pos]) → identical value written. Inner guard (pos<size) prevents OOB. All positions 0..size-1 covered correctly.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation causes threads to process one additional position (i=4 instead of stopping at i=3), which overlaps with the starting position of the next thread's work. However, both the original write and the redundant write compute the identical value: hardtanh_activation(input[pos], min_val, max_val). Since this function is deterministic and both threads read the same input position, the race condition is benign. The inner bounds check `if (pos < size)` prevents any out-of-bounds access at the tensor boundary. This makes the mutant functionally equivalent to the original for all possible input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable because it produces bitwise identical output for all input values. The redundant writes are idempotent (same value written by both racing threads). No value-level test can distinguish between original and mutant.
rounds.recommendations: When testing loop bound mutations (< vs <=), verify whether the extra iteration produces semantically different values or just redundant identical writes. Equivalent mutants can arise when overlapping work regions compute identical results. Consider adding assertions for write uniqueness in debug builds to catch such benign races during development.
